questions.question: A metallic solid spherical ball of radius 3 cm is melted and recast into three spherical balls. The radii of two of these balls are 2 cm and 1.5 cm. What is the surface area (in cm²) of the third ball?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In melting and recasting, Total Volume remains constant: R³ = r₁³ + r₂³ + r₃³

3³ = 2³ + 1.5³ + r₃³ ⇒ 27 = 8 + 3.375 + r₃³

r₃³ = 27 − 11.375 = 15.625 ⇒ r₃ = 2.5 cm

Surface Area of third ball = 4 π r₃² = 4 × π × (2.5)² = 25 π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 25 π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of large ball (R) = 3 cm

Radii of two small balls: r₁ = 2 cm, r₂ = 1.5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of Sphere = (4/3) π r³

Surface Area of Sphere = 4 π r²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/48d543782cff3b785207a5c8bc8048bd64589cecd8d4ee0237d90f87eca5ac68.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of Original Ball = Volume of Ball 1 + Volume of Ball 2 + Volume of Ball 3

⇒ (4/3) π R³ = (4/3) π r₁³ + (4/3) π r₂³ + (4/3) π r₃³

⇒ R³ = r₁³ + r₂³ + r₃³

⇒ 3³ = 2³ + (1.5)³ + r₃³

⇒ 27 = 8 + 3.375 + r₃³

⇒ 27 = 11.375 + r₃³

⇒ r₃³ = 27 − 11.375 = 15.625

⇒ r₃ = √³(15.625) = 2.5 cm

⇒ Surface Area of the third ball = 4 π r₃²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × (2.5)²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × 6.25

⇒ Surface Area = 25 π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 25 π cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume and Surface Area of a Sphere

For a sphere of radius r, the Volume V = (4/3) π r³ and Total Surface Area S = 4 π r².

Hemisphere Formulas

Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) π r³. Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2 π r². Total Surface Area (TSA) = 3 π r².

Conservation of Volume

When a solid is melted and recast into other shapes, the total volume remains constant, provided there is no wastage during the process.</p

questions.question: ((1 + tantheta + sectheta)(1 + cottheta - cosectheta))/((sectheta + tantheta)(1 - sintheta)) is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use substitution method: Let θ = 30°.

Numerator = (1 + tan 30° + sec 30°)(1 + cot 30° − cosec 30°) = (1 + 1/√3 + 2/√3)(1 + √3 − 2) = (1 + √3)(√3 − 1) = 2.

Denominator = (sec 30° + tan 30°)(1 − sin 30°) = (2/√3 + 1/√3)(1 − 1/2) = (3/√3) × (1/2) = √3/2.

Expression = 2 ÷ (√3/2) = 4/√3.

Check options: 2sec 30° = 2 × (2/√3) = 4/√3, which matches the result.

**∴ The correct answer is 2secθ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [(1 + tanθ + secθ)(1 + cotθ − cosecθ)] ÷ [(secθ + tanθ)(1 − sinθ)]

**Formula Used:** tanθ = sinθ/cosθ; cotθ = cosθ/sinθ; sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c7b9efab81968cac2a14d09209fd4a5232ca4b92c05fc945b1d735ef466151e.png] 

Solving Numerator:

⇒ (1 + sinθ/cosθ + 1/cosθ) × (1 + cosθ/sinθ − 1/sinθ)

⇒ [(cosθ + sinθ + 1)/cosθ] × [(sinθ + cosθ − 1)/sinθ]

⇒ [(sinθ + cosθ)² − 1²] / (sinθ × cosθ)

⇒ (sin²θ + cos²θ + 2sinθcosθ − 1) / (sinθcosθ) = 2sinθcosθ / sinθcosθ = 2

Solving Denominator:

⇒ (1/cosθ + sinθ/cosθ) × (1 − sinθ)

⇒ [(1 + sinθ)/cosθ] × (1 − sinθ) = (1 − sin²θ) / cosθ

⇒ cos²θ / cosθ = cosθ

Final Value:

⇒ 2 ÷ cosθ = 2secθ

**∴ The correct answer is 2secθ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Identities

Standard identities like sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1 are crucial for simplification.

Value Substitution Method

For trigonometric expressions where options are also in trigonometric form, substituting values like 30°, 45°, or 60° can save time, provided no denominator becomes zero.

Reciprocal Relations

Always remember: secθ = 1/cosθ, cosecθ = 1/sinθ, and tanθ = sinθ/cosθ to convert complex terms into basic sine and cosine.</p

questions.question: A train travelling at 36 km/h crosses a pole in 25 seconds. How much time (in seconds) will it take to cross a bridge 250 m long?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed in m/s = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

Length of Train = Speed × Time = 10 × 25 = 250 m.

Total Distance to cross bridge = Train length + Bridge length = 250 + 250 = 500 m.

Required Time = Total Distance ÷ Speed = 500 ÷ 10 = 50 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of train = 36 km/h

Time to cross pole (t₁) = 25 seconds

Length of bridge (Lb) = 250 m

**Formula Used:**

Speed (m/s) = Speed (km/h) × 5/18

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efbfb650d51951222ec3400bac645da6c15c0ffb63207cc377eda947802d4ca4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of train = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

⇒ Length of train (Lₜ) = Speed × Time to cross pole

⇒ Lₜ = 10 × 25 = 250 m

⇒ Total distance to cross bridge = Lₜ + Lb

⇒ Total distance = 250 + 250 = 500 m

⇒ Time to cross bridge = Total distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Time = 500 ÷ 10 = 50 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 50 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. In opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Crossing Stationary Objects

Total distance = Length of train + Length of object (If object is a point like a pole or man, its length is taken as 0).</p

questions.question: Alloy A contains metals x and y only in the ratio 5 : 2 and alloy B contains these metals in the ratio 3 : 4. Alloy C is prepared by mixing A and B in the ratio 4 : 5. The percentage of x in alloy C is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of ratio parts in A (5+2) and B (3+4) is 7 (equal).

Mixed in ratio A : B = 4 : 5.

Total units of x = (4 × 5) + (5 × 3) = 20 + 15 = 35 units.

Total quantity of Alloy C = (4 + 5) × 7 = 63 units.

Percentage of x in C = (35 ÷ 63) × 100 = (5 ÷ 9) × 100 = 55 5/9 %.

**∴ The correct answer is 55 5/9 %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of x : y in Alloy A = 5 : 2

Ratio of x : y in Alloy B = 3 : 4

Mixing ratio A : B = 4 : 5

**Formula Used:**

Percentage of a component = (Quantity of component ÷ Total quantity) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe560a55426d1553aa1dbbf241e031c683a882030dd9a9c835b3d566da228cd0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total parts in A = 5 + 2 = 7; Total parts in B = 3 + 4 = 7.

⇒ Let we take 4 units of A and 5 units of B (mixing ratio 4:5).

⇒ Quantity of x in A = (5 ÷ 7) × 4 = 20 ÷ 7

⇒ Quantity of x in B = (3 ÷ 7) × 5 = 15 ÷ 7

⇒ Total quantity of x in C = (20 ÷ 7) + (15 ÷ 7) = 35 ÷ 7 = 5 units

⇒ Total quantity of C = 4 + 5 = 9 units

⇒ Percentage of x in C = (5 ÷ 9) × 100

⇒ Percentage of x in C = 500 ÷ 9 = 55.55... %

⇒ Percentage of x in C = 55 5/9 %

**∴ The correct answer is 55 5/9 %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Method

When two mixtures are mixed in ratio m:n, the average concentration is (m × c₁ + n × c₂) ÷ (m + n).

Alligation Rule

Ratio of quantities = (Cheaper price − Mean price) : (Mean price − Dearer price), used to find mixing proportions.

Fraction to Percentage Conversion

To convert a fraction a/b to percentage, multiply by 100. Common fractions: 1/9 = 11 1/9 % and 5/9 = 55 5/9 %.</p

questions.question: To do a certain work, the ratio of the efficiencies of A and B is 7 : 5. Working together, they can complete the same work in 17 (1)/(2) days. A alone will complete 60% of the same work in:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency Ratio A : B = 7 : 5 → Total Efficiency (A + B) = 12 units/day.

Total Work = Combined Efficiency × Combined Time = 12 × 17.5 = 210 units.

Required Work = 60% of Total Work = 0.60 × 210 = 126 units.

Time for A alone = Required Work ÷ Efficiency of A = 126 ÷ 7 = 18 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Efficiency of A : Efficiency of B = 7 : 5

Time taken by A and B together = 17 1/2 days = 35/2 days

Calculations:

⇒ Let the efficiency of A be 7x and B be 5x.

⇒ Total efficiency of (A + B) = 7x + 5x = 12x.

⇒ Total Work = Efficiency × Time = 12x × 35/2 = 6x × 35 = 210x units.

⇒ 60% of the work = 60/100 × 210x = 126x units.

⇒ Time taken by A alone to do 60% work = 126x ÷ 7x = 18 days.

**__Additional Information__**

Work and Efficiency Relationship

Work is directly proportional to both Efficiency and Time (Work = E × T). If work is constant, Efficiency is inversely proportional to Time taken.

Efficiency Ratio

If the ratio of time taken by A and B is x : y, then the ratio of their efficiencies is 1/x : 1/y or y : x.

Combined Efficiency

When people work together, their efficiencies are additive. Total Efficiency = Efficiency₁ + Efficiency₂ + ... + Efficiencyₙ.</p

questions.question: Amita travels from her house at 3 (1)/(2) km/h and reaches her school 6 minutes late. The next day she travels at 4 (1)/(2)km/h and reaches her school 10 minutes early. What is the distance between her house and the school?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed 1 (S₁) = 3.5 km/h, Speed 2 (S₂) = 4.5 km/h.

Total time difference = 6 min (late) + 10 min (early) = 16 minutes = 16/60 hours.

Distance = (S₁ × S₂) / (S₂ − S₁) × Time Difference

Distance = (3.5 × 4.5) / (4.5 − 3.5) × (16 / 60)

Distance = (15.75 / 1) × (4 / 15) = 1.05 × 4 = 4.2 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.2 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Speed = 3.5 km/h, Final Speed = 4.5 km/h.

Time 1 = 6 minutes late, Time 2 = 10 minutes early.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/424bedbce67090182091f465613262f4ef01639a2c0d1919d136143507c670d3.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Total time difference (ΔT) = (Late + Early) / 60 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance between house and school be D km.

⇒ ΔT = (6 + 10) / 60 = 16 / 60 = 4 / 15 hours.

⇒ (D / 3.5) − (D / 4.5) = 4 / 15

⇒ (4.5D − 3.5D) / (3.5 × 4.5) = 4 / 15

⇒ D / 15.75 = 4 / 15

⇒ D = (4 × 15.75) / 15

⇒ D = 63 / 15 = 4.2 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.2 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time Difference Calculation

When comparing late and early arrivals, if one is late and one is early, add the times. If both are late or both are early, subtract the smaller time from the larger time.

Ratio Method for Fixed Distance

If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁). The difference in time units can be equated to the actual time difference to find the distance.

Average Speed for Two Equal Distances

When a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × x × y) / (x + y).</p

questions.question:
The circumference of the base of a cylindrical vessel is 158.4 cm and its height is 1 m. How many litres of water can it hold (correct to one decimal place)?

(Take pi = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Calculate radius directly from circumference: r = Circumference ÷ (2 × π) = 158.4 ÷ 6.2857 ≈ 25.2 cm.

Volume in cm³ = πr²h = (22/7) × (25.2)² × 100.

Convert to litres (1 litre = 1000 cm³): Volume = [22/7 × 635.04 × 100] ÷ 1000.

Volume = 199584 ÷ 1000 = 199.584 litres.

Rounding to one decimal place, we get 199.6 litres.

**∴ The correct answer is 199.6 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Circumference of base = 158.4 cm

Height (h) = 1 m = 100 cm

π = 22/7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee47ead52d024332e314aedbb91afce2a6d5fb42d513c73414c2e8fa3d73f6ef.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Circumference = 2 × π × r

Volume of Cylinder = π × r² × h

1 Litre = 1000 cm³

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 158.4

⇒ r = (158.4 × 7) ÷ (2 × 22)

⇒ r = (158.4 × 7) ÷ 44

⇒ r = 3.6 × 7 = 25.2 cm

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × (25.2)² × 100

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 25.2 × 25.2 × 100

⇒ Volume = 22 × 3.6 × 25.2 × 100

⇒ Volume = 79.2 × 2520 = 199584 cm³

⇒ Capacity in Litres = 199584 ÷ 1000

⇒ Capacity = 199.584 litres ≈ 199.6 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 199.6 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The area of the side surface is given by CSA = 2 × π × r × h.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The area of all surfaces including top and bottom: TSA = 2 × π × r × (r + h).

Volume and Capacity Units

1 m³ = 1000 litres; 1 litre = 1000 cm³; 1 cm³ = 1 ml.</p

questions.question: The compound interest on a sum of Rs. 20,000 at 15% p.a. for 2 (2)/(3)years, when interest compounded yearly is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate for the first 2 years is 15% p.a. and for the next 2/3 year, the rate is 15% × 2/3 = 10%.

Net percentage rate for 2 years = 15 + 15 + (15 × 15)/100 = 32.25%.

Total compound interest percentage for 2 2/3 years = 32.25 + 10 + (32.25 × 10)/100 = 42.25 + 3.225 = 45.475%.

Compound Interest = 20,000 × 45.475% = 20,000 × 0.45475 = ₹9,095.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,095.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹20,000

Rate (R) = 15% p.a.

Time (T) = 2 2/3 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R/100)ⁿ × (1 + (R × f)/100), where n is the whole year and f is the fraction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6ddd2a7984b2756ce3fc1979602f171cce6a51c645abc9be1429e417e183b0f.png] 

⇒ For the first 2 years, Rate = 15%

⇒ For the remaining 2/3 year, Rate = 15 × 2/3 = 10%

⇒ Amount (A) = 20,000 × (1 + 15/100) × (1 + 15/100) × (1 + 10/100)

⇒ A = 20,000 × (115/100) × (115/100) × (110/100)

⇒ A = 20,000 × 1.15 × 1.15 × 1.1

⇒ A = 20,000 × 1.3225 × 1.1

⇒ A = 26,450 × 1.1 = ₹29,095

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

⇒ CI = 29,095 − 20,000 = ₹9,095

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,095.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI for Fractional Time

When time is in fractions like t = n (a/b) years, Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ × (1 + (R × a/b)/100).

Effective Rate for Successive Years

If interest rates for different years are R₁, R₂, and R₃, the effective multiplier is (1 + R₁/100)(1 + R₂/100)(1 + R₃/100).

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is given by CI − SI = P(R/100)².

In ΔPRQ, ∠P = 90° , S and T are the mid points of sides PR and PQ respectively. What is the value of RQ²/(QS² + RT²)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, if QS and RT are medians drawn to the legs from the acute angles, then:

4 × (QS² + RT²) = 5 × RQ² (where RQ is the hypotenuse)

Rearranging the formula: RQ² / (QS² + RT²) = 4 / 5

**∴ The correct answer is 4/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠P = 90°, S is the midpoint of PR, T is the midpoint of PQ.

**Formula:** Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a0cb2448058f6d69d5c7e045e3c975faece0be0fcbaac9db7b9c1290697904c.png] 

⇒ In ΔPRQ: RQ² = PR² + PQ²

⇒ In ΔPQS: QS² = PQ² + PS²

⇒ Since S is midpoint of PR, PS = PR/2 ∴ QS² = PQ² + (PR/2)² = PQ² + PR²/4

⇒ In ΔPRT: RT² = PR² + PT²

⇒ Since T is midpoint of PQ, PT = PQ/2 ∴ RT² = PR² + (PQ/2)² = PR² + PQ²/4

⇒ QS² + RT² = (PQ² + PR²/4) + (PR² + PQ²/4)

⇒ QS² + RT² = 5/4 × PQ² + 5/4 × PR² = 5/4 × (PQ² + PR²)

questions.question: In ΔABC, right angled at B, if tanA = 1/2, then the value of (sin A(cos C + cos A))/(cos C (sin C - sin A)) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled ΔABC at B, A and C are complementary angles, meaning A + C = 90°.

This implies sin A = cos C and cos A = sin C.

Substitute these into the expression: [sin A(sin A + cos A)] ÷ [sin A(cos A − sin A)]

The sin A terms cancel out, simplifying the expression to (sin A + cos A) ÷ (cos A − sin A).

Divide the numerator and denominator by cos A to get: (tan A + 1) ÷ (1 − tan A).

Substituting tan A = 1/2: (0.5 + 1) ÷ (1 − 0.5) = 1.5 ÷ 0.5 = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: In ΔABC, ∠B = 90° and tan A = 1/2.

Formula: tan A = Perpendicular ÷ Base = BC ÷ AB.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f07528dee15425112be1bf82bf04887a0841d9e3b7eeea3bbd2d3b643dd6726f.png] 

⇒ Let BC = 1 and AB = 2.

⇒ By Pythagoras Theorem: AC = √(AB² + BC²) = √(2² + 1²) = √5.

⇒ For ∠A: sin A = BC/AC = 1/√5 and cos A = AB/AC = 2/√5.

⇒ For ∠C: sin C = AB/AC = 2/√5 and cos C = BC/AC = 1/√5.

⇒ Expression = [sin A(cos C + cos A)] ÷ [cos C (sin C − sin A)]

⇒ Expression = [(1/√5) × (1/√5 + 2/√5)] ÷ [(1/√5) × (2/√5 − 1/√5)]

⇒ Expression = [(1/√5) × (3/√5)] ÷ [(1/√5) × (1/√5)]

⇒ Expression = (3/5) ÷ (1/5) = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

In a right triangle where A + C = 90°, sin A = cos C, cos A = sin C, tan A = cot C, and sec A = cosec C.

Tangent Addition Formula

The expression (1 + tan A) ÷ (1 − tan A) is equivalent to tan(45° + A).

Pythagorean Triplet Basics

For any right triangle, Perpendicular² + Base² = Hypotenuse². Here, 1² + 2² = (√5)².</p

questions.question: The number of students in section A and section B of a class are 40 and 52, respectively. The average score in mathematics of all the students is 75. If the average score of the students in A is 20% more than that of students in B, then what is the average score of students in B?

Ratio of students (A : B) = 40 : 52 = 10 : 13

Ratio of average scores (A : B) = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5

Weighted average parts = (10 × 6 + 13 × 5) ÷ (10 + 13) = 125/23 parts

Given, 125/23 parts = 75 ⇒ 1 part = (75 × 23) ÷ 125 = 13.8

Average score of students in B = 5 × 13.8 = 69 marks

**Given:**

Number of students in A (nA) = 40

Number of students in B (nB) = 52

⇒ Average score of students in A = x + 20% of x = 1.2x

⇒ Total sum of scores = (40 × 1.2x) + (52 × x)

⇒ Average = Sum ÷ Count ⇒ 75 = (48x + 52x) ÷ 92

⇒ 75 = 100x ÷ 92

⇒ 100x = 75 × 92

⇒ 100x = 6900

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups is given by Aₐvg = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the number of items and a is the individual average.

Alligation Rule

The ratio of the quantities is inversely proportional to the deviation of their averages from the mean average: n₁ ÷ n₂ = (a₂ − Aₐvg) ÷ (Aₐvg − a₁).

questions.question: If cosec θ = b/a, then frac{sqrt{3} cot theta + 1}{tan theta + sqrt{3}} is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Simplify the expression: (√3 cot θ + 1) / (tan θ + √3)

⇒ [(√3 / tan θ) + 1] / (tan θ + √3)

⇒ [(√3 + tan θ) / tan θ] / (tan θ + √3) = 1 / tan θ = cot θ

Given cosec θ = b/a, we know cot θ = √(cosec² θ − 1)

⇒ cot θ = √((b/a)² − 1) = √(b² − a²) / a

**∴ The correct answer is √(b² − a²)/a.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cosec θ = b/a

**Formula Used:** cosec θ = Hypotenuse / Perpendicular | cot θ = Base / Perpendicular

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/80ccad0c59f327ea27e085a0980801c9a730a7547b1de4cfebc82475510c344f.png] 

Let Perpendicular = a and Hypotenuse = b

⇒ Base² = Hypotenuse² − Perpendicular²

⇒ Base = √(b² − a²)

Now, evaluate the given expression E:

⇒ E = (√3 cot θ + 1) / (tan θ + √3)

⇒ E = (√3 × (Base/Perp) + 1) / ((Perp/Base) + √3)

Alternatively, simplifying the expression algebraically:

⇒ E = (√3 cot θ + 1) / (1/cot θ + √3)

⇒ E = (√3 cot θ + 1) / [(1 + √3 cot θ) / cot θ]

⇒ E = [(√3 cot θ + 1) × cot θ] / (√3 cot θ + 1)

⇒ E = cot θ

⇒ cot θ = Base / Perpendicular = √(b² − a²) / a

**∴ The correct answer is √(b² − a²)/a.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The three fundamental identities are sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

Reciprocal Relationships

The ratios are linked by: cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = 1/tan θ.

Pythagoras Theorem

In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides: H² = P² + B².</p

questions.question: The base of a solid right prism of height 10 cm is a square and its volume is 160 cm³. What is its total surface area of the prism (in cm²)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**192**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• A **right prism** is a three-dimensional solid where the bases are congruent polygons and the lateral faces are rectangles. In this question, the base is a **square** and the height is 10 cm.

• The **volume** of a prism is given by the formula: **Volume = Area of Base × Height**.

• Given, Volume = 160 cm³ and Height (h) = 10 cm. Let the side of the square base be 'a'.

• Area of the square base = a².

• Substituting the values: 160 = a² × 10.

• a² = 16, which means side **a = 4 cm**.

• The **Total Surface Area (TSA)** of a prism is calculated as: **TSA = (2 × Area of Base) + (Perimeter of Base × Height)**.

• **Area of Base** = a² = 4² = 16 cm².

• **Perimeter of Base** (Square) = 4 × a = 4 × 4 = 16 cm.

• Now, calculate **TSA**: (2 × 16) + (16 × 10) = 32 + 160 = **192 cm²**.

• Thus, the total surface area of the prism is **192 cm²**, which matches **Option 3**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Lateral Surface Area (LSA)** of a prism is the area of its side faces only, calculated as: **LSA = Perimeter of Base × Height**. In this case, LSA = 16 × 10 = 160 cm².

• For any **regular prism**, the total surface area always includes the sum of the lateral area and the areas of the two bases (top and bottom).

• The unit of **volume** is always in cubic units (e.g., cm³), while the unit of **area** is always in square units (e.g., cm²).

questions.question: A cylindrical roller made of iron is 1.2 m long. Its internal radius is 24 cm and thickness of the iron sheet used in making the roller is 15 cm. What is the mass (in kg) of the roller, if 1 cm³ of iron has 8 g mass?

Outer radius R = Internal radius + Thickness = 24 + 15 = 39 cm.

Length of roller h = 1.2 m = 120 cm.

Thickness of iron = 15 cm

questions.question: If x - (1)/(x) = 5, x neq 0, then what is the value of (x⁶ + 3x³ - 1)/(x⁶ - 8x³ - 1)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Divide the numerator and denominator of the expression by x³.

The expression becomes: [(x³ − 1/x³) + 3] / [(x³ − 1/x³) − 8].

Given x − 1/x = 5, use the shortcut x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k = 5³ + 3(5) = 140.

Substitute 140: (140 + 3) / (140 − 8) = 143 / 132.

On simplifying by 11, we get 13/12.

**∴ The correct answer is 13/12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: x − 1/x = 5

Formula used: (a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)

⇒ (x − 1/x)³ = x³ − (1/x)³ − 3(x)(1/x)(x − 1/x)

⇒ 5³ = x³ − 1/x³ − 3(5)

⇒ 125 = x³ − 1/x³ − 15

⇒ x³ − 1/x³ = 125 + 15 = 140

Required expression: (x⁶ + 3x³ − 1) / (x⁶ − 8x³ − 1)

⇒ Dividing numerator and denominator by x³:

⇒ [(x⁶/x³) + (3x³/x³) − (1/x³)] / [(x⁶/x³) − (8x³/x³) − (1/x³)]

⇒ (x³ + 3 − 1/x³) / (x³ − 8 − 1/x³)

⇒ [(x³ − 1/x³) + 3] / [(x³ − 1/x³) − 8]

⇒ (140 + 3) / (140 − 8)

⇒ 143 / 132

⇒ 13/12

**∴ The correct answer is 13/12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Cubing Identities

For any non-zero x, if x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k. Conversely, if x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k.

Algebraic Squaring Identities

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2. If x + 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² − 2.

Rational Symmetry

In expressions involving x²ⁿ and xⁿ, dividing the entire expression by xⁿ often reveals a symmetric form related to (x + 1/x) or (x − 1/x).</p
